## INTAKE QA FOUNDING-COHORT PILOT — MEMORANDUM OF UNDERSTANDING

Between **Plaintiff Ops LLC** ("Intake QA") and **____________________** ("Firm"),
effective _____________.

### 1. What the pilot is

A free evaluation of Intake QA's post-call intake review service, for a fixed window of
**90 days** from the Kickoff Date. Intake QA will:

- ingest intake-call recordings the Firm already makes (export, shared folder, or a
  one-time phone-system connection — no change to how the Firm answers calls);
- transcribe and score each call against a personal-injury intake rubric;
- flag likely-lost signable cases in a **daily rescue packet** (the flagged calls, why
  they were flagged, and a suggested callback script for the Firm's staff);
- maintain a **recovered-case ledger**: when the Firm confirms a flagged lead signed, the
  ledger records it at the Firm's own valuation.

### 2. What the pilot is not (scope limits — these are contractual)

- **Intake QA never contacts the Firm's callers, clients, or prospective clients.** Every
  callback is made by the Firm's own staff. Intake QA is a quality-control vendor to the
  Firm, not a marketer, referral source, or intermediary.
- **Intake QA gives no legal advice** to anyone, and nothing in its packets or scripts is
  legal advice; the Firm exercises independent professional judgment on every lead.
- **No outcome-tied fees, ever.** The pilot is free. If the Firm converts after the pilot,
  pricing is a **flat monthly subscription** — never a percentage of fees, never per-case,
  never tied to recoveries (Rule 5.4).
- No changes to the Firm's phone system, CRM, or case-management software are required or
  made during the pilot.

### 3. The Firm's part (about 15 minutes a day)

- Provide recordings (or authorize the one-time connection) and confirm that its recording
  practice includes all-party consent notice as California law requires (§5 below).
- Have a named staff member act on the daily packet: attempt the flagged callbacks and
  record the outcome (reached / signed / passed) in the desk.
- Confirm or correct ledger entries; join a 15-minute check-in around day 30 and a
  decision meeting by day 90.
- Baseline: at kickoff, the Firm shares its approximate monthly call volume, current
  signing rate if known, and average fee on a routine case, so the pilot is measured
  against a real baseline.

### 4. The success metric and the decision

One number decides the pilot: **confirmed recovered fee value on the ledger** — cases the
Firm agrees it would otherwise have lost, valued by the Firm. At the day-90 meeting the
Parties review the ledger; if it clearly exceeds the subscription cost, the expectation is
conversion at the founding-cohort rate of $________/month flat (locked for ____ months).
Either Party may end the pilot at any time with written notice; there is no obligation to
convert.

### 5. Recording consent (CIPA)

The Firm represents that call recordings it provides were made with the notice/consent
California law requires (Penal Code §632 et seq.). Intake QA records no calls itself and
analyzes only recordings the Firm lawfully made. If the Firm's recording notice is not in
place, the Parties will limit the pilot to prospective recordings made after corrected
notice.

### 6. Data handling

Firm audio and transcripts are handled under the signed NDA and Intake QA's Data
Processing Addendum: named subprocessors (AssemblyAI for transcription, Anthropic for
analysis) under no-model-training terms; deletion on request and at offboarding; no
caller PII in URLs, logs, or analytics. A BAA is available if the Firm requires one.

### 7. Feedback and reference

The Firm agrees to give honest feedback on utility and user experience (that's the point
of a beta). At the Firm's option — never required — a successful pilot may conclude with a
testimonial or anonymized case study; nothing will be published without the Firm's written
approval of the exact text.

### 8. General

This MOU is a statement of mutual intent for the pilot; the only binding provisions are §2
(scope limits), §5 (consent representation), §6 (data handling), the NDA, and the DPA. No
partnership, referral arrangement, or fee-sharing is created. California law; venue Los
Angeles County.

## Reviewer notes (Yang)

1. §2 is written to keep the service on the right side of B&P §6152/SB 37 (no claimant
   contact, no procurement) and Rule 5.4 (flat fee) — confirm the language is airtight.
2. §4 names a conversion price but creates no obligation — confirm "expectation is
   conversion" reads as intent, not a binding option.
3. §5 puts the CIPA representation on the Firm, where the recording happens — confirm.
4. Day-90 window chosen over 60 to let signed PI cases mature (playbook: extend once,
   not indefinitely).
